brief_angle: When a museum deletes its wall labels, does the information actually disappear or just migrate — and does the deaf visitor end up in a more level room, or in a room whose default channel has quietly become speech (docents, tours, audio guides) with text demoted to atmosphere?
notes: Aphorism budget is over. You have at least three verdict-sentences competing: 'Migration is not demotion. It can be the opposite.' / 'One is authorship. The other is abdication dressed as generosity.' / and the closing 'moved the translator's mouth closer.' Three crescendos means none land. Keep the last one — the closing image is the strongest and earns its place — and flatten the other two into plain prose. 'Migration is not demotion' especially reads as a manufactured beat; let the Cleveland scene make that point without the epigram stamped on it.

Signposted moves: cut 'That broke my thesis.' and cut 'Which is where the thing I keep circling gets uncomfortable.' Both announce the turn instead of letting it turn. The Cleveland material and the Christine Sun Kim material already do the work — the reader feels the thesis break and feels the discomfort without being told a break and a discomfort are coming. Delete the announcements, leave the material.

The Christine Sun Kim thread is your best complication — a deaf artist from inside deaf culture throwing out the neutral label you want to defend — but in the final third you resolve it too tidily with 'the difference is who holds the pen.' That resolution lets the argument absorb its own strongest objection; Kim ends up serving your thesis rather than resisting it. Consider letting the Kim tension stay live rather than reconciled, so the piece keeps the friction it actually earned. Protect what's genuinely working, though: the ArtLens discovery ('I opened it... and it handed me more written context than any wall in that building has ever offered') is a real past-tense moment of being wrong, and Dawn Reid Brean's quote is a genuine voice the narrator did not script — do not sand either of those down in revision.
